It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the "unsearchable riches" of Christ while witnessing the "noise and tumult" of a world where nations seek to erase the "vestiges of Christian religion" by the "wholesale transformation" of sacred geography, and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the ruins of our buildings and the silence of desecrated sanctuaries in this hour? [1, 16, 754, 1503, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling "overwhelmed and desperate" because the "divine standards and biblical morality that our nation once embraced are assaulted constantly," or are you seeking a "settled certainty" to anchor your soul in the truth that the "gates of hell" cannot prevail against the true Church, even when every stone is turned over? [17, 21, 89, 1422, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many "shave off the edges" of the truth to find "diplomatic relations" with an "anti-Christian agenda," we must return to the "external Word" to see how the Master personally provides for the "repose of the soul" by recognizing that "His counsel shall stand, and He will do all His pleasure" [11, 17, 28, 1428, 1493, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that "God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation," and therefore, the erasure of a place of worship is not an "administrative anomaly" but is subject to the "decree from God" who "works all things according to the counsel of His own will" [15, 170, 174, 503, 1494, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: God’s Sovereignty Over Desolated Kingdoms**

**Verse**
“ ‘Remember the former things of old, For I am God, and there is no other; I am God, and there is none like Me, Declaring the end from the beginning, And from ancient times things that are not yet done, Saying, “My counsel shall stand, And I will do all My pleasure” ’ ” (Isaiah 46:9–10). [1493, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed faith—echoed by **John MacArthur**—asserts that "not one human sinner or demonic power will ever succeed in his rebellion" against the King of kings, for He "raises up kings, then pulls them from their thrones when they have served His administration" [175, 503, 1307, 1484, Conversation History]. When nations "lay your cities waste and bring your sanctuaries to desolation," they are often acting as an "instrument of God’s vengeance" or a "staff in whose hand is My indignation" to test the hearts of His people (Leviticus 26:31; Isaiah 10:5) [760, 798, 1090, Conversation History]. Even the "worst atrocity ever carried out"—the Cross—proves that the "deeds of the wicked" are harnessed to "accomplish His good and perfect ends," meaning that the destruction of a building is never the destruction of His "sovereign plan" [5, 1490, 1495, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should "trade in your worry for trust," for "nothing thwarts any aspect of His plan," and the "Word of our God stands forever" regardless of the fate of any human "building enterprise" (Isaiah 40:8) [21, 94, 1306, 1307, 1343, 1408, 1495, 1515, Conversation History]. "Wait for His Son from heaven," knowing that "God has numbered your kingdom and put an end to it" for every "oppressor" who thinks they are "better than they really are" (Daniel 5:26) [24, 25, 210, 1315, 1408, 1515, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Continuity of the Decree**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, "national greatness" and "large and beautiful cities" were seen as "temporal signs" of God's favor, yet Israel was warned that if they "acted corruptly," they would "utterly perish from the land" (Deuteronomy 4:25–26) [409, 500, 1353, 1519, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our posture, teaching that while "the present form of this world is passing away," we look for a "city whose builder and maker is God" (1 Corinthians 7:31; Hebrews 11:10) [24, 126, 1592, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: Biblical Lament Over Desecrated Sanctuaries**

**Verse**
“Your holy cities are a wilderness, Zion is a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation. Our holy and beautiful temple, Where our fathers praised You, Is burned up with fire; And all our pleasant things are laid waste” (Isaiah 64:10–11). [600, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Scripture reveals that it is not a sin to feel a "broken heart" over the desolation of "holy cities" and the "removal of God’s immediate presence," for "Jeremiah lived the majority of his life in frustration and confusion, all the while weeping" (Jeremiah 9:1) [4, 849, 1365, Conversation History]. The "record of history" contains "symbols of grief and isolation," such as the cry " ‘Unclean! Unclean!’ " heard from the survivors of Jerusalem’s destruction (Lamentations 4:15) [1390, Conversation History]. Yet, even in the "horrible pit" of desolation, the faithful "extol the glory, name, and works of God," recognizing that "through the Lord’s mercies we are not consumed" (Lamentations 3:22) [4, 472, 1440, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should "not be deceived" by a "no-lordship ideology" that tells you to be indifferent to the loss of sacred things; rather, "confess your own utter spiritual poverty" and "implore His mercy" (Psalm 145:1–3) [11, 49, 89, 91, 153, 1169, 1403, 1502, Conversation History]. You can find "tranquility of soul" by "resting upon the surest foundation," knowing that "the Lord knows those who are His" and He will "respond to the prayer of the destitute" (2 Timothy 2:19; Psalm 102:17) [11, 24, 88, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 300, 324, 361, 405, 414, 444, 591, 1138, 1143, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Ritual vs. Reality**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, "man-made representations" were "incinerated" as "strange fire" if they were not built according to the "divine instructions" (Leviticus 10:1–2) [9, 237, 239, 241, 1344, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our "sacred" focus, showing that "God, our Savior, ‘desires all men to be saved’ ” and "the mission" is "to lead people destined to spend eternity in hell to a saving knowledge," which is a priority that transcends the bricks of a sanctuary (1 Timothy 2:4) [19, 39, 53, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: The Revision of the Sanctuary (Building vs. Body)**

**Verse**
“Or do you not know that your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God, and you are not your own?” (1 Corinthians 6:19). [11, 1119, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Voddie Baucham** and **Paul Washer**—teaches that the "true church" is an "intangible and invisible" spiritual house where "the presence and glory of God" are manifested through the "sanctified" lives of His people [11, 17, 355, 402, 1153, 1219, 1251, 1313, 1426, Conversation History]. While we are saddened by the "noise and tumult" of destroyed buildings, we recognize that "the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands" (Acts 7:48) [11, 142, 612, 1042, 1316, 1646, Conversation History]. The "wholesale transformation" of the believer means that you act as a "portable temple," carrying "in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus" so that his life may be seen in you even when the sanctuary is gone (2 Corinthians 4:10) [11, 469, 790, 1503, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
"Never become so involved in this world" that you seek "deliverance" from a "legislative body" rather than from the "Rock of Ages," for "your life is not your own" because you were "bought at a price" (1 Corinthians 6:20) [12, 51, 101, 130, 212, 415, 1138, 1262, 1503, 1623, 1670, Conversation History]. Your "sole objective" is to "adorn the doctrine of God" and "be holy in all your behavior," for your "citizenship is in heaven" (1 Peter 1:15; Philippians 3:20) [13, 14, 26, 31, 38, 101, 142, 361, 1188, 1320, 1342, 1406, 1426, 1450, 1502, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: From Ritual to Reality**
Under the **Mosaic Law**, "testifying in a dispute" required "witnesses" and strict "safeguards" regarding the physical sanctuary [330, 367, 499, 1072, 1230, 1317, 1365, 1473, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our "victory," teaching that "the church militant" conquers not through "carnal weaponry" but “by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony,” ensuring that the true Temple is indestructible (Revelation 12:11) [13, 21, 32, 92, 956, 1313, 1402, 1491, 1515, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The Final Triumph and the Everlasting Temple**

**Verse**
“Then the seventh angel sounded: And there were loud voices in heaven, saying, ‘The kingdoms of this world have become the kingdoms of our Lord and of His Christ, and He shall reign forever and ever!’ ” (Revelation 11:15). [152, 650, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The biblical authors resolve the "noise and tumult" of "troublesome times" and "desolations" by fixating on the "consummation of history," where "Christ ultimately crushes the kingdoms of men and establishes His own" [13, 20, 21, 23, 103, 136, 815, 1199, 1315, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. In the "new redeemed heaven and earth," there is "no temple" because "the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple" (Revelation 21:22) [449, 454, 652, Conversation History]. Every earthly "monument of pride" and "storage city" will "vanish—like smoke they vanish away," but the "people who have been made righteous by Christ himself" will dwell in His presence forever (Psalm 102:3; Revelation 21:4) [11, 32, 43, 452, 470, 789, 903, 1260, 1315, 1460, 1684, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
"Wait for His Son from heaven," knowing that "perfect justice will come" and he will "wipe away every tear from their eyes" (1 Thessalonians 1:10; Revelation 21:4) [14, 24, 94, 109, 201, 224, 459, 1315, 1408, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. You should find "tranquility of soul" by "resting upon the surest foundation," for if God has "magnified Your word above all Your name," His "everlasting dominion" is "secure" (Psalm 138:2; Daniel 7:14) [11, 24, 47, 92, 121, 176, 201, 352, 386, 412, 1132, 1143, 1408, 1420, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 300, 332, 405, 414, 444, 591, 1138, 1450, Conversation History].

references.cited_text: The Fear of the Lord Is Not an Option The psalmist asked, “Who may dwell on Your holy hill?” (Ps. 15:1). The answer is simply, “He who walks with integrity, and works righteousness, and speaks truth in his heart” (v. 2). There is no greater need today than for believers once again to ascend the platform of fearing God. A. W. Tozer said it well: “No religion has been greater than its idea of God.” That gem has a corollary: No church is greater than its reverent awe of holy God. He is holy and demands recognition as such. Although most believers know that intellectually, I’m afraid very few realize what that means practically.
